title: CPR (adult cardiac arrest)
dispatcher_summary: Adult unresponsive and not breathing normally; bystander CPR in progress.
clarifying_question: Is the person awake and responding, and are they breathing normally?

steps.text: Tap the person's shoulders and shout "Are you OK?"
steps.spoken: Tap their shoulders and shout. Are they responding?

steps.text: Call emergency services (or have someone call) and get an AED.
steps.spoken: Call 911 now, or tell someone nearby to call and bring an AED.

steps.text: Place the person on their back on a firm surface. Kneel beside the chest.
steps.spoken: Lay them flat on their back on a firm surface and kneel beside their chest.

steps.text: Place the heel of one hand on the center of the chest, other hand on top, arms straight.
steps.spoken: Put the heel of one hand on the center of the chest, other hand on top, arms straight.

steps.text: Push hard and fast, at least 2 inches (5 cm) deep, 100-120 compressions per minute. Let the chest fully recoil.
steps.spoken: Push hard and fast in the center of the chest. Follow the beat. Let the chest rise fully each time.

steps.text: When an AED arrives, turn it on and follow its voice prompts.
steps.spoken: When the defibrillator arrives, turn it on and follow its instructions.

steps.text: Continue until the person responds, an AED advises otherwise, or responders take over.
steps.spoken: Keep going until help arrives or the person starts moving.

source: AHA/Red Cross adult hands-only CPR guidance (to be verified by reviewer)
